articles.title: DHS’ 4-year cap on student visa stays struck down by federal judge
articles.summary: A federal judge struck down the Department of Homeland Security’s four-year cap on student visa stays. The judge ruled that the law does not grant DHS broad and open-ended authority to undermine the student visa program.
articles.insight:
This ruling temporarily removes a restrictive U.S. visa policy, potentially improving perceived stability and long-term study prospects for international students—though broader U.S. visa processing delays, costs, and post-study work rules remain dominant demand drivers across all destination countries.  
Admissions teams should track whether this decision leads to measurable increases in U.S.-bound applications from key markets like India or China, while continuing to benchmark against UK, Australia, and New Zealand’s evolving post-study work and dependant policies.

articles.title: UKVI rejects 80% of students called to interview as visa refusals surge
articles.summary: New data obtained by The PIE shows that UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) rejected 79% of prospective international students who were called for a credibility interview over a six-month period. This high refusal rate coincides with an overall surge in student visa refusals.
articles.insight:
This news signals potential tightening of UK student visa scrutiny, which may dampen UK appeal for risk-averse applicants—though it’s unclear whether this reflects broader policy shifts or temporary operational factors affecting applicant selection.  
Admissions teams should monitor UK refusal trends by nationality and qualification type, while reviewing pre-application support to ensure documentation rigor aligns with heightened credibility expectations.

articles.title: US court strikes down rule that would have ended Duration of Status (D/S) for international students
articles.summary: On 16 November 2026, a U.S. federal judge in the District of Massachusetts struck down the Department of Homeland Security’s final rule that would have eliminated the Duration of Status (D/S) policy for international students, exchange visitors, and foreign media representatives. The court ruled the rule was “arbitrary and capricious” under the Administrative Procedure Act.
articles.insight:
This ruling preserves the current D/S framework for F-1, J-1, and I visa holders, potentially sustaining enrolment confidence among prospective students from high-volume regions like India, China, and Nigeria—though broader immigration policy uncertainty and economic factors remain stronger demand drivers than this single litigation outcome.  
Admissions teams should track subsequent DHS appeals or revised regulatory proposals, while updating compliance training and advising agents on stable D/S validity—no immediate policy changes are expected, but continued vigilance on U.S. visa adjudication trends and competitor messaging is prudent.

articles.title: Vietnamese student enrollment in US hits record high despite overall decline
articles.summary: Nearly 27,300 Vietnamese students are currently studying in the United States, the highest number ever recorded. This figure represents growth for Vietnam despite an overall decline in international student enrollment in the U.S.
articles.insight:
Vietnam’s record-high enrollment amid broader U.S. international student declines suggests growing relative appeal—potentially driven by scholarship access, bilateral education ties, or shifting perceptions of U.S. visa stability—though causality remains unclear without granular data on visa issuance rates or cohort-specific motivations.  
Admissions teams should track Vietnamese applicants’ program preferences, funding sources, and post-study work uptake trends, while benchmarking against peer institutions’ recruitment investments in Vietnam to assess whether sustained growth warrants expanded local outreach or partnership development.

articles.title: US Open Doors 2026: Why Indian student enrolments are falling even as post-study work numbers surge
articles.summary: The Open Doors 2026 report shows Indian graduate student enrolments in the US fell 34.4% to 116,609 in 2025–26, while the number of Indian students on Optional Practical Training (OPT) rose 26.8% to a record 182,201. Although India remains the largest source of international students in the US, declining new enrolments, visa challenges, rising costs, and global competition are affecting Indian postgraduate study abroad trends.
articles.insight:
The sharp drop in new Indian graduate enrolments—despite rising OPT participation—suggests potential shifts in timing, pathway preferences, or destination diversification, though it remains unclear whether this reflects temporary visa processing delays, strategic deferrals, or deeper erosion of US appeal for initial study.  
Admissions teams should track Indian student applications across entry points (e.g., foundation, undergraduate, direct PhD), monitor OPT-to-H-1B transition rates and UK/Australia post-study work policy updates, and assess whether service partners report changing counselling narratives around US value proposition.

articles.title: Du học sinh Việt đến Mỹ đông kỷ lục giữa làn sóng sụt giảm
articles.summary: Nearly 27,300 Vietnamese students are studying in the United States, the highest number on record. This growth contrasts with an overall decline in international student enrollment in the U.S.
articles.insight:
Vietnamese student enrollment in the U.S. reaching a record 27,300—amid broader international declines—suggests sustained demand from this high-performing Southeast Asian market, though it remains unclear whether this reflects unique policy advantages, scholarship uptake, or shifting regional preferences rather than a broad trend reversal.  
Admissions teams should track Vietnamese application volumes, visa approval rates, and competitor activity in Vietnam—including U.S. institutions’ recruitment investments and messaging—while benchmarking against peer destinations to assess relative appeal and inform targeted outreach adjustments.

articles.title: Campus France recebe inscrições para brasileiros estudarem na França em 2027
articles.summary: Campus France is currently accepting applications from Brazilian students who wish to pursue undergraduate or master’s degree programs in France starting in 2027. The announcement was published on November 18, 2026, at 6:00 a.m.
articles.insight:
This news signals potential shifts in Brazilian student preferences toward European destinations, possibly reflecting evolving perceptions of affordability, post-study work opportunities, or geopolitical factors—though it remains unclear whether this represents a structural trend or short-term response to specific policy changes in France or competing countries.  
Admissions teams should monitor Brazilian application volumes and enrolment trends over the next 12–18 months, particularly for undergraduate and master’s programs, while reviewing their value propositions on cost, career outcomes, and visa stability relative to France’s updated offerings.

articles.title: Shoolini and Edinburgh partner on engineering degrees across India and the UK
articles.summary: Shoolini University and the University of Edinburgh have partnered to offer joint engineering degree programs spanning India and the UK. Students will study engineering in both countries, with Shoolini subsidising the program and strengthening teaching and research collaboration with Edinburgh.
articles.insight:
This partnership signals growing demand for transnational engineering education, potentially reflecting Indian students’ increasing preference for globally recognised degrees with mobility—though it remains unclear whether this will divert applicants from traditional Anglophone destinations or instead raise overall aspiration levels.  
Admissions teams should monitor uptake and graduate outcomes of this programme, as well as any policy shifts in UK-India academic collaboration or student visa pathways, to assess whether similar dual-location models could strengthen their own value proposition in the Indian market.

articles.title: Canada announces targets for new international student arrivals through 2029
articles.summary: The Canadian government announced temporary immigration targets for 2027, 2028, and 2029 as part of the 2027–2029 Immigration Levels Plan, released on 5 November alongside the federal budget. The plan sets an annual cap of 370,000 permits for new international student arrivals to support sustainable immigration, stability, predictability, and economic growth.
articles.insight:
Canada’s 370,000-per-year cap on new international student permits signals a deliberate shift toward managed growth, which may indirectly influence global student mobility patterns—though demand shifts in other destinations will depend on how source markets perceive Canada’s stability versus competing nations’ policy consistency and post-study opportunities.  
Admissions teams should monitor real-time application trends from key shared source markets (e.g., India, Nigeria, Philippines), track visa processing times and refusal rates in Canada, and assess whether its tightened controls create modest near-term opportunity to reinforce their own value propositions around employability and regulatory clarity.
